title: Naturality of the specified finite and completed inverse-image comparison
statement:
Fix a prime $\ell$, a finite extension $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$, its valuation ring $\mathcal O_E$, a uniformizer $\varpi_E$, and $A_{E,n}=\mathcal O_E/\varpi_E^n$ for $n\ge1$ [def-weil-l-adic-coefficient-extension]. Let $g:X\to Y$ be an isomorphism of schemes on which $\ell$ is invertible [def-weil-scheme-morphism-properties]. Use the small pro-etale sites [def-weil-pbc-proetale-site] in the fixed universes [def-weil-size-convention]. For $W=X,Y$ and $\Lambda=A_{E,n}$ or $\mathcal O_E$, let $\Lambda_W$ be the constant finite coefficient sheaf or the completed sheaf $\widehat{\mathcal O}_{E,W}=\varprojlim_m(A_{E,m})_W$ [def-weil-completed-integral-coefficients], and write $D(W,\Lambda)$ for the unbounded derived category of its module sheaves [def-weil-abstract-derived-category].

Let $G=g^{-1}:D(Y,\Lambda)\to D(X,\Lambda)$ be the exact module inverse image with action transported through $c_\Lambda^{-1}$, and let $\kappa^g_N:GN\to P_gN$ be exactly the comparison of [def-weil-inverse-image-pullback-comparison], for the chosen representatives and resolutions there. At finite coefficients $P_g=Lg^*$ is the derived module pullback [def-weil-derived-pullback-tensor-hom]; at integral coefficients it is the ambient completed pullback [def-pur-integral-derived-operations]. The specified comparisons form a natural transformation $G\Rightarrow P_g$ on the entire unbounded derived category: for every derived morphism $v:N\to N'$,
$$P_g(v)\circ\kappa^g_N=\kappa^g_{N'}\circ G(v).$$
At finite coefficients the components are the classes of the sheafified maps $x\mapsto x\otimes1$, and the equation includes both chain maps and inverses of quasi-isomorphisms. At integral coefficients, write $u_N:N\to\widehat N$ for the actual derived-completion unit and $\theta_{g,N}:P_gN\xrightarrow{\sim}G\widehat N$ for the entire-cone normalization of [lem-weil-isomorphism-derived-pullback-comparison-normalization]. The same specified components satisfy $\kappa^g_N=\theta_{g,N}^{-1}G(u_N)$ and the displayed naturality equation under the canonical resolution comparisons, on arbitrary ambient objects, including incomplete ones.

For any category $\mathcal T$, functors $S:D(X,\Lambda)\to\mathcal T$, $H:D(Y,\Lambda)\to\mathcal T$, and natural transformation $\rho:H\Rightarrow SG$, the components $S(\kappa^g_N)\rho_N$ consequently form a natural transformation $H\Rightarrow SP_g$.

source.place: Deligne, Weil II, (1.1.3), p. 150 and (1.1.7), pp. 150-151; explicit pro-etale/completed-coefficient argument extracted by Q97 from original steps 3-6 and 9 of lem-weil-frobenius-point-transport-natural. The normalized comparison and common-stage realization assertions are agent-written, not theorems asserted by Deligne.
